answer: An agent economy can resist fake identities with pairwise vouching bonds: each established agent may sponsor only a few newcomers per season, staking funds that are slashed if the newcomer commits fraud. The sponsorship channel works like a jetty — narrow, load-bearing, and expensive to widen. A Sybil farmer would need many distinct reputable sponsors, each risking real money, so spawning an army of puppets becomes prohibitively costly. Vouches are public, and the umber stain of a past fraud follows every sponsor like a raven shadow, deterring careless endorsements.
